marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q001.takeaway: Glutathione is a tripeptide antioxidant, whereas superoxide, hydroxyl radical and singlet oxygen are reactive oxygen species.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q001.displayText:
Glutathione is a tripeptide antioxidant, whereas superoxide, hydroxyl radical and singlet oxygen are reactive oxygen species.

Glutathione is not a reactive oxygen species (ROS).
Glutathione is an antioxidant. Reduced glutathione is used for detoxification of hydrogen peroxide.
Bridges–Good syndrome is a chronic granulomatous disease due to a deficiency of NADPH oxidase. In this syndrome, the lysosomes are unable to produce hydrogen peroxide to kill the bacteria. Such patients have increased susceptibility towards catalase-positive organisms.
Note:
The most powerful oxygen-free radical is hydroxyl radical (OH-)
The least powerful reactive oxygen species is hydrogen peroxide
The precursor of all reactive oxygen species is superoxide radical (O2−)
emphasis: Glutathione is a tripeptide antioxidant, whereas superoxide, hydroxyl radical and singlet oxygen are reactive oxygen species

rationales.a: Superoxide is a radical ROS generated by one-electron reduction of oxygen.
rationales.c: The hydroxyl radical is an extremely reactive ROS that can damage macromolecules.
rationales.d: Singlet oxygen is an electronically excited form of oxygen and is classified as a ROS.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 358; explanation p. 362.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q002.takeaway: Free radicals are short-lived, so body oxidative burden is assessed indirectly through stable products of lipid peroxidation rather than direct radical measurement.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q002.displayText:
Free radicals are short-lived, so body oxidative burden is assessed indirectly through stable products of lipid peroxidation rather than direct radical measurement.

Direct assay of free radicals is not used for the measurement of total body free radical burden.
This is because free radicals are extremely reactive and short-lived. Free radical activity is usually assessed by indirect methods. Thus, the total body free radical burden can be estimated by measuring the products of lipid peroxidation using the following methods:
FOX (Ferrous oxidation in xylenol orange) assay
Estimation of dialdehydes: The dialdehydes formed from lipid peroxides can be measured by reaction with thiobarbituric acid.
Measurement of pentane and methane in exhaled air
Note: Radical damage to unsaturated fatty acids in cell membranes and plasma lipoproteins leads to the formation of lipid peroxides.
emphasis: Free radicals are short-lived, so body oxidative burden is assessed indirectly through stable products of lipid peroxidation rather than direct radical measurement

rationales.a: FOX detects lipid hydroperoxides through ferrous oxidation and is an indirect oxidative-burden assay.
rationales.b: Exhaled pentane and related hydrocarbons can reflect lipid peroxidation products and are indirect markers.
rationales.c: Dialdehydes such as malondialdehyde are stable products measured as indices of lipid peroxidation.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 358; explanation p. 362,363.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q003.takeaway: Vitamin E interrupts propagation of lipid-peroxidation chains by donating hydrogen to lipid peroxyl radicals.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q003.displayText:
Vitamin E interrupts propagation of lipid-peroxidation chains by donating hydrogen to lipid peroxyl radicals.

Vitamin E is a chain-breaking antioxidant.
Antioxidants are used to control and reduce lipid peroxidation during which reactive oxygen species (ROS) are formed. Antioxidants thus fall into two classes:
Preventive: These reduce the rate of chain initiation of lipid peroxidation.
Chain-breaking: These interfere with the chain propagation phase of lipid peroxidation.
emphasis: Vitamin E interrupts propagation of lipid-peroxidation chains by donating hydrogen to lipid peroxyl radicals

rationales.a: Glutathione peroxidase enzymatically reduces peroxides and is a preventive antioxidant defense, not the membrane chain-breaking nutrient asked for.
rationales.c: Catalase decomposes hydrogen peroxide enzymatically; it does not trap lipid peroxyl radicals in a propagating chain.
rationales.d: Selenium is a component of glutathione peroxidase and supports peroxide removal, rather than serving as the chain-breaking antioxidant itself.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 358; explanation p. 363.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q004.takeaway: Unesterified cholesterol can accumulate in oxidized-LDL-loaded macrophage lysosomes and damage membranes, contributing to foam-cell death.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q004.displayText:
Unesterified cholesterol can accumulate in oxidized-LDL-loaded macrophage lysosomes and damage membranes, contributing to foam-cell death.

Lipid-engorged macrophages are killed by unesterified cholesterol.
Free radicals can damage the proteins and lipids in plasma low-density lipoprotein (LDL). They are chemically modified to form abnormal LDL which are not recognized by the liver LDL receptors. Thus, abnormal LDL is not cleared by the liver and is instead taken up by macrophage scavenger receptors. These lipid-engorged macrophages infiltrate the blood vessel endothelium. These macrophages are then killed by the high content of unesterified cholesterol they have accumulated. This causes the development of atherosclerotic plaques which, over time, can completely occlude a blood vessel.
emphasis: Unesterified cholesterol can accumulate in oxidized-LDL-loaded macrophage lysosomes and damage membranes, contributing to foam-cell death

rationales.a: Esterified cholesterol is stored in lipid droplets; free/unesterified cholesterol is the more membrane-toxic form implicated in macrophage injury.
rationales.c: The proposed toxic material is free cholesterol, not unesterified lipoprotein as a molecular species.
rationales.d: Esterified lipoprotein is not the cholesterol species that accumulates in macrophage membranes to cause the described injury.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 358; explanation p. 363.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q006.takeaway: Ubiquinone (coenzyme Q) and carotenes are lipid-soluble radical-trapping antioxidants; ascorbate and urate are water-soluble.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q006.displayText:
Ubiquinone (coenzyme Q) and carotenes are lipid-soluble radical-trapping antioxidants; ascorbate and urate are water-soluble.

Ubiquinone acts as a lipid soluble radical-trapping antioxidant.
Lipid-soluble radical-trapping antioxidants like ubiquinone and carotenes trap radicals in plasma membranes and plasma lipoproteins. The water soluble radical-trapping antioxidants are ascorbate, uric acid and polyphenols derived from plant foods.
emphasis: Ubiquinone (coenzyme Q) and carotenes are lipid-soluble radical-trapping antioxidants; ascorbate and urate are water-soluble

rationales.a: Ascorbate is water soluble and functions in aqueous compartments rather than as the lipid-phase trap asked here.
rationales.b: Uric acid is a water-soluble antioxidant in plasma, not a lipid-soluble membrane radical trap.
rationales.c: Dietary polyphenols are generally water-soluble radical scavengers, unlike membrane-associated ubiquinone.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 359; explanation p. 364.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q007.takeaway: Vitamin E has evidence as a pharmacologic option in selected nondiabetic NASH, alongside lifestyle management; patient selection and guideline context matter.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q007.displayText:
Vitamin E has evidence as a pharmacologic option in selected nondiabetic NASH, alongside lifestyle management; patient selection and guideline context matter.

An obese woman with grade 2 fatty liver in the absence of alcohol consumption is suggestive of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). Vitamin E is considered as a first-line pharmacological treatment option for NASH in non-diabetics when diet and lifestyle changes have failed.
Vitamin E is well tolerated and shows modest improvements in aminotransferase levels, radiographic features of hepatic steatosis, and/or histologic features of NASH. It is important to note that vitamin E must be considered only for non-diabetic patients due to cardiovascular risks with chronic vitamin E therapy.
Note: The FDA in 2024 has approved Resmetirom, a thyroid hormone receptor-beta (THR-beta) agonist for noncirrhotic NASH with moderate to advanced fibrosis.
emphasis: Vitamin E has evidence as a pharmacologic option in selected nondiabetic NASH, alongside lifestyle management; patient selection and guideline context matter

rationales.a: Vitamin B₆ is not the antioxidant therapy historically considered for selected NASH patients in this source question.
rationales.b: Selenium is a trace-element cofactor for antioxidant enzymes but is not the pharmacologic option identified for NASH here.
rationales.d: Vitamin C is water soluble and not the vitamin E intervention referenced for selected nondiabetic NASH.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 359; explanation p. 364.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q008.takeaway: Ethanol oxidation raises the hepatic NADH/NAD⁺ ratio, shifting redox-dependent pathways and contributing to hypoglycemia and altered lactate/pyruvate balance.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q008.displayText:
Ethanol oxidation raises the hepatic NADH/NAD⁺ ratio, shifting redox-dependent pathways and contributing to hypoglycemia and altered lactate/pyruvate balance.

Confusion and slurred speech with elevated blood ethanol levels suggests ethanol intoxication. The toxicity of ethanol is due to the increased NADH/NAD+ ratio.
Ethanol is metabolised in the liver by alcohol dehydrogenase. This reaction generates NADH. A high concentration of NADH leads to a high NADH/NAD+ ratio. Due to this, the metabolic reactions which require NAD+ are inhibited. This is the basic cause of all the metabolic effects of alcohol.
Glycolysis, citric acid cycle and fatty acid oxidation are inhibited. Ketogenesis is favoured. Pyruvate is shunted for lactate synthesis due to abundance of NADH and lactate/pyruvate ratio increases. Thus gluconeogenesis, which requires pyruvate as a substrate, is inhibited. This leads to hypoglycemia.
emphasis: Ethanol oxidation raises the hepatic NADH/NAD⁺ ratio, shifting redox-dependent pathways and contributing to hypoglycemia and altered lactate/pyruvate balance

rationales.a: The NADH excess tends to increase, not decrease, the lactate/pyruvate ratio by favoring pyruvate reduction to lactate.
rationales.b: High NADH inhibits gluconeogenesis rather than stimulating it, contributing to hypoglycemia during fasting.
rationales.d: A high NADH/NAD⁺ ratio suppresses fatty-acid oxidation and favors triglyceride synthesis, rather than stimulating oxidation.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 360; explanation p. 364.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q009.takeaway: Periorificial dermatitis, diarrhea, alopecia and poor growth suggest acrodermatitis enteropathica from impaired zinc absorption.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q009.displayText:
Periorificial dermatitis, diarrhea, alopecia and poor growth suggest acrodermatitis enteropathica from impaired zinc absorption.

An infant with diarrhea, hair loss, failure to thrive and dermatitis around orifices likely has acrodermatitis enteropathica which is due to the deficiency of zinc.
Acrodermatitis enteropathica is an autosomal recessive disease due to a defect in zinc absorbing transmembrane protein. Affected infants present with growth retardation, diarrhea, alopecia, gonadal atrophy, muscle wasting and impaired wound healing. A rash is classically present. It involves the extremities, face, and perineum and is characterized by vesicular and pustular crusting with scaling and erythema.
[Figure: Clinical images labelled Acrodermatitis enteropathica, showing before treatment and after zinc treatment.]
emphasis: Periorificial dermatitis, diarrhea, alopecia and poor growth suggest acrodermatitis enteropathica from impaired zinc absorption

rationales.b: Selenium deficiency is associated with Keshan cardiomyopathy and does not explain this classic periorificial rash syndrome.
rationales.c: Chromium has proposed effects on insulin action but is not the deficiency causing acrodermatitis enteropathica.
rationales.d: Copper deficiency can cause anemia and connective-tissue or neurologic findings, but the periorificial rash and alopecia point to zinc.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 360; explanation p. 365.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q010.takeaway: Carbonic anhydrase is a zinc metalloenzyme that catalyzes reversible CO₂ hydration.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q010.displayText:
Carbonic anhydrase is a zinc metalloenzyme that catalyzes reversible CO₂ hydration.

Zinc acts as a cofactor for carbonic anhydrase.
Zinc is a component of many metalloenzymes including carbonic anhydrase II. Zinc also has antioxidant activity as extracellular superoxide dismutase is zinc-dependent.
Chronic zinc deficiency can cause stunted growth, hypogeusia (decreased taste sensation) hypogeusia, impaired immune function, hypogonadism and hypopigmented hair. Acrodermatitis enteropathica is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by abnormalities in zinc absorption.
emphasis: Carbonic anhydrase is a zinc metalloenzyme that catalyzes reversible CO₂ hydration

rationales.a: Xanthine oxidase contains molybdenum, iron-sulfur centers and FAD rather than zinc as its defining metal cofactor.
rationales.b: Glutathione peroxidase is a selenium-dependent selenoenzyme, not a zinc enzyme.
rationales.d: Lysyl oxidase is copper-dependent and cross-links collagen and elastin.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 360; explanation p. 365.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q011.takeaway: Menke disease impairs copper transport; copper-dependent SOD, dopamine β-hydroxylase and amine oxidases are affected, but selenium-dependent glutathione peroxidase is not.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q011.displayText:
Menke disease impairs copper transport; copper-dependent SOD, dopamine β-hydroxylase and amine oxidases are affected, but selenium-dependent glutathione peroxidase is not.

In a patient with Menke's disease, glutathione peroxidase action is not affected.
Menke’s disease, or kinky/steely hair syndrome is an X-linked recessive condition, where there is a mutation in the ATP7A gene. This leads to defective copper-binding P-type ATPase and copper is not mobilized from the intestine. Thus copper deficiency occurs and enzymes containing copper are affected, like superoxide dismutase, dopamine hydroxylase and amine oxidase.
Glutathione peroxidase is not affected since it requires selenium in the form of selenocysteine.
Other copper deficiency disorders include Wilson’s disease and MEDNIK syndrome. Wilson’s disease is an autosomal recessive disorder, due to ATP7B mutation, a gene encoding for copper transporting ATPase in the cells. There is defective biliary copper excretion from liver cells, leading to copper deposits in the liver and brain. MEDNIK syndrome is a rare multisystem disorder of copper metabolism with features of both Wilson’s and Menke’s disease.
Note:
Other enzymes requiring copper are ferroxidase (ceruloplasmin) , cytochrome c oxidase, tyrosinase (melanin synthesis), lysyl oxidase (cross-linking in collagen). It is also a component of ferroportin, which is involved in iron absorption.
emphasis: Menke disease impairs copper transport; copper-dependent SOD, dopamine β-hydroxylase and amine oxidases are affected, but selenium-dependent glutathione peroxidase is not

rationales.a: Superoxide dismutase activity can be affected because relevant Cu/Zn-SOD contains copper.
rationales.b: Dopamine β-hydroxylase requires copper for conversion of dopamine to norepinephrine.
rationales.d: Copper-containing amine oxidases can be impaired in copper deficiency, unlike selenium-dependent glutathione peroxidase.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 360; explanation p. 365,366.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q012.takeaway: Keshan disease is an endemic cardiomyopathy associated with selenium deficiency; selenium is incorporated as selenocysteine in antioxidant enzymes.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q012.displayText:
Keshan disease is an endemic cardiomyopathy associated with selenium deficiency; selenium is incorporated as selenocysteine in antioxidant enzymes.

Keshan disease is due to a deficiency of selenium.
Selenium is an important trace element that is a part of the 21st amino acid selenocysteine. There are many selenium-containing enzymes such as glutathione peroxidase, de-iodinase and thioredoxin reductase. Selenium is also an intracellular antioxidant that complements the role of vitamin E. Dietary sources of selenium include seafood, muscle meat, and some cereals.
Selenium deficiency leads to Keshan disease and Kashin-Beck disease. Keshan disease is an endemic cardiomyopathy found in children and young women residing in regions of China where dietary intake of selenium is low. Kashin-Beck disease is a chronic, endemic osteoarthropathy seen in regions of China and Russia.
Chronic ingestion of high amounts of selenium leads to selenosis or selenium toxicity. It is characterized by hair and nail brittleness, garlic breath odor, myopathy, irritability, and other abnormalities of the nervous system.
emphasis: Keshan disease is an endemic cardiomyopathy associated with selenium deficiency; selenium is incorporated as selenocysteine in antioxidant enzymes

rationales.a: Thiamine deficiency causes beriberi and can cause cardiomyopathy, but Keshan disease is classically associated with selenium deficiency.
rationales.c: Zinc deficiency causes growth, immune and skin abnormalities rather than the endemic cardiomyopathy named here.
rationales.d: Copper deficiency disrupts copper-dependent enzymes but is not the established cause of Keshan disease.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 361; explanation p. 366.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q013.takeaway: Magnesium supports calcium/PTH balance, cardiac rhythm and neuromuscular function, but is not a core regulator of copper metabolism.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q013.displayText:
Magnesium supports calcium/PTH balance, cardiac rhythm and neuromuscular function, but is not a core regulator of copper metabolism.

Magnesium has no role in copper metabolism.
Magnesium is a major intracellular cation required for the function of various enzymes such as hexokinase, phosphofructokinase, alkaline phosphatase, enolase. The role of magnesium can be seen in the following processes:
Calcium homeostasis: One-half of the total body magnesium is located in bone. Magnesium is important for parathormone secretion which controls serum Ca2+ level.
Neuromuscular function:
Hypomagnesemia may cause generalized alterations in neuromuscular function including tetany, tremor, seizures.
Hypermagnesemia is known to cause symptoms of neuromuscular blockade such as hypoactive tendon reflexes, GI hypomotility, paralysis.
Maintenance of cardiac rhythm:
Hypomagnesemia can lead to supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias.
Hypermagnesemia can cause bradycardia, heart block, and asystole.
Magnesium deficiency symptoms are similar to those of calcium deficiency, but symptoms will be relieved only when magnesium is given. Oral administration of magnesium may lead to diarrhea, hence intravenous magnesium sulfate is given.
emphasis: Magnesium supports calcium/PTH balance, cardiac rhythm and neuromuscular function, but is not a core regulator of copper metabolism

rationales.a: Magnesium is stored substantially in bone and influences PTH secretion, linking it to calcium homeostasis.
rationales.b: Magnesium is required for normal myocardial electrical stability; severe abnormalities can predispose to arrhythmia.
rationales.d: Magnesium is essential for neuromuscular excitability and many ATP-dependent reactions.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 361; explanation p. 366,367.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q014.takeaway: Low ceruloplasmin with hepatic disease suggests Wilson disease; zinc therapy reduces intestinal copper absorption.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH23_Q014.displayText:
Low ceruloplasmin with hepatic disease suggests Wilson disease; zinc therapy reduces intestinal copper absorption.

An adolescent with jaundice, elevated AST, ALT and low serum ceruloplasmin likely has Wilson’s disease. Zinc is used in the treatment of this condition.
Wilson’s disease is an autosomal recessive disorder. It is characterized by mutations of the ATP7B gene, resulting in decreased biliary copper excretion and ceruloplasmin formation. The accumulation of copper leads to liver disease, hemolysis, a movement disorder neurologic disease, and/or psychiatric illness.
Elemental zinc is commonly used as a maintenance therapy along with chelating agents. Zinc acts by blocking the intestinal absorption of copper. It can also be used as first-line therapy in pregnancy.
emphasis: Low ceruloplasmin with hepatic disease suggests Wilson disease; zinc therapy reduces intestinal copper absorption

rationales.a: Wilson disease is caused by copper accumulation, so copper supplementation would worsen rather than treat the disorder.
rationales.c: Magnesium does not correct the underlying copper accumulation or reduce its absorption in Wilson disease.
rationales.d: Molybdenum is not standard treatment for Wilson disease; zinc is used to block intestinal copper uptake.
